evidence.observation: All ten second-round sources have stable intake and source IDs, public-safe descriptions, dispositions, and explicit links to claims or inquiries. Unverified memories remain deferred research leads.

Each promoted source records provenance, review metadata, locators, affirmative support, and explicit non-support. Coalition-authored, journalistic, and government sources retain distinct evidentiary roles.
Organizer role, attributed signup count, advocacy, town-hall participation, testimony, campaign interface, and legislative outcome are separate claims with individual boundaries and anti-claims.

Every selected FairRentNYC claim resolves through the page plan to canonical claims and public sources. The generated registry preserves those relationships without exposing protected source paths or private artifacts.

Knowledge maturity, publication safety, editorial selection, and projection status remain independent. Confirmed but unused Office, March 2018, priorities, and Save NYC Spaces material is not automatically projected.

The dossier situates the corpus across early organizing, Cabaret Law advocacy, Office of Nightlife accountability, town halls, affordability testimony, and Talks Not Raids, with collective-credit boundaries and future photo-research prompts.

The more-than-100 count remains explicitly attributed to Jamie rather than audited. Event scale, exact production shares, Office-creation causality, M.A.R.C.H. disbandment, and final Cabaret enactment evidence remain openly unresolved.

The page selects eight purposeful claims supported by nine sources, using seven of the ten new sources while retaining three as contextual or unused research. Institutional outcomes are stated separately from advocacy activity and causal credit. Jamie's documented actions are visible without converting coalition accomplishments into solo achievements, and no protected material is exposed.
